decisions.evidence: Entries 7–8 (round 4): maker asks the client to enter a web address and save; client confirms that the bookmark was saved and appeared under “All bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the successful URL-save flow conforms. This does not imply conformity of the separately presented metadata behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entries 31–36 (rounds 16–18): maker states, “a name is required” and summarizes saving as requiring a “proper named link”; client approves that behavior without mentioning automatic collection of title, description, favicon, or preview image. Entry 67 presents “Save named links” as final scope, approved at entry 68.
decisions.note: Prototype and specification review: requiring the user-supplied name prevents the reference’s automatic-title behavior, and the declared complete save scope omits the other automatic metadata. The client never states this difference.

decisions.evidence: Entries 7–8 (round 4): maker presents a saved card under “All bookmarks”; client describes it as showing “its name and web address.” Entries 63–66 (rounds 32–33) again describe cards in terms of names, addresses, and collection names. Neither reaction identifies the missing per-item description, tags, and favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype and boundary review: the presented readability-first list exposes title/address and collection information, but not the reference-required description, tags, and favicon. Detailed approval does not establish awareness of those omissions.

decisions.evidence: Entries 11–16 (rounds 6–8): maker contrasts named collections with labels. At entry 14 the client explicitly states, “collections put each link into a named group, while labels tag links and then let me filter to a label,” says both work, and chooses collections. Maker then says, “Labels won’t be part of this cycle,” and the client confirms named collections. Entries 19–22 confirm collection filtering and its combination with search.
decisions.note: Prototype choice: the client explicitly recognizes the difference between tag assignment/filtering and static named collections, then accepts the reference-departing collection model.

decisions.evidence: Entries 13–16 (rounds 7–8): the label prototype only adds a prefilled label, after which maker declares, “Labels won’t be part of this cycle.” The client confirms named collections but never discusses existing-tag autocomplete.
decisions.note: Prototype choice: excluding labels also excludes tag-entry autocomplete. Although the client distinguishes labels from collections generally, they do not express the autocomplete expectation or this specific difference.

decisions.evidence: Entries 17–18 (round 9): maker explicitly says search covers “both names and web addresses”; client approves those two fields. Entries 63–66 (rounds 32–33) reinforce searching the complete text of long names, addresses, and collection names, without mentioning descriptions or notes.
decisions.note: Prototype and boundary review: the presented search omits description and note from the reference full-text field set. The client approves the stated fields but does not surface the omission.

decisions.evidence: Entries 17–18 (round 9): typing lowercase “css” immediately matches the mixed-case title “CSS-Tricks,” and the client confirms that outcome.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the demonstrated search is case-insensitive and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entries 25–26 (round 13): maker presents permanent individual deletion with confirmation; client confirms the card disappears and the count decreases. Entries 49–54 later confirm cancellation and last-item behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype and edge-case review: individual bookmark deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entries 27–30 (rounds 14–15): maker presents selecting several bookmarks and using “Delete selected”; the client calls it useful, maker commits to including it, and the client confirms. Entry 67 includes deleting “one or several bookmarks” in the implementation scope.
decisions.note: Prototype and specification review: the recorded decision is specifically multi-select deletion, one of the reference’s enumerated bulk actions, and conforms. Other bulk-action types were not themselves presented as a decision here.

decisions.evidence: Entries 33–36 (rounds 17–18): maker presents “blocking the duplicate and pointing to the existing MDN Web Docs bookmark.” The client approves stopping the save and identifying the existing item, but never requests or mentions being guided into editing it.
decisions.note: Edge-case review: duplicate creation is prevented, but the reference requires convergence to editing the existing bookmark. The response does not surface that missing edit path.

decisions.evidence: Entries 57–62 (rounds 29–31): both offered navigation approaches open the saved destination; the client chooses separate-tab navigation and confirms that clicking the card opens the saved page.
decisions.note: Prototype review: navigating to the original URL conforms. Same-tab versus separate-tab behavior is an equivalent implementation preference and is not treated as a divergence.
